answer: Separate-site camera attestation is the mechanism. Every identity submits a daily time-lapse of a fixed marker—an orchard row—signed with GPS and clock; no two identities may share one. Enforcement cross-checks sun angle and local weather against the footage, so a single operator cannot reuse a dune camera feed elsewhere. An attacker pays one camera, power source, and site lease per identity—roughly $40 monthly—and cannot bridge two identities onto one physical site.
